sovereign_country.strategic_role: 全球供应链制造母港、跨境电商货源地与外资合规准入市场

business_scope.primary_industry_name: Digital Advertising Media Arbitrage and Affiliate Lead Gen

meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Hybrid (Common Law heritage with local statutory overlay, distinct from Mainland China civil law)
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Agreement between the Government of the People's Republic of China and the Government of the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region for the Avoidance of Double Taxation and the Prevention of Fiscal Evasion with Respect to Taxes on Income (DTA)
Mainland and Hong Kong Closer Economic Partnership Arrangement (CEPA)
Agreement on Investment between the Government of the People's Republic of China and the Government of the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region (under CEPA framework)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Anti-Money Laundering and Counter-Terrorist Financing Ordinance (Cap. 615, Laws of Hong Kong) as amended; Companies Ordinance (Cap. 622) for UBO register requirements; PBOC/SAMR Order No. 3 (effective Nov 1, 2024) for Mainland China UBO disclosure; Hong Kong Monetary Authority (HKMA) Guideline on Anti-Money Laundering and Counter-Financing of Terrorism (for banks); Securities and Futures Commission (SFC) AML/CFT guidelines for licensed corporations.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incorporation (CoI) of the Hong Kong holding company
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille: Issued by Hong Kong Companies Registry -> Apostille certificate from the High Court of Hong Kong (Designated Competent Authority under the Apostille Convention) -> No further consular legalization required for Mainland China (as China is a member of the Apostille Convention, but note: Mainland China acceded to the Apostille Convention on Nov 7, 2023, effective Nov 7, 2023; however, for documents originating from Hong Kong, the apostille is issued by the High Court of Hong Kong and accepted in Mainland China).

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing (CoGS) from Hong Kong Companies Registry
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille: Issued by Hong Kong Companies Registry -> Apostille from High Court of Hong Kong -> Accepted in Mainland China without consular legalization.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Board Resolution or Power of Attorney (PoA) authorizing the WFOE incorporation and nominee director appointments
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Hong Kong holding company board of directors
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarization by Hong Kong Notary Public -> Apostille from High Court of Hong Kong -> Accepted in Mainland China.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Articles of Association (AoA) of the Hong Kong holding company
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Certified true copy by Companies Registry -> Apostille from High Court of Hong Kong -> Accepted in Mainland China.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank Reference Letter from the Hong Kong holding company's principal bank
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Licensed bank in Hong Kong (e.g., HSBC, Standard Chartered)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarization by bank officer -> Apostille from High Court of Hong Kong -> Accepted in Mainland China.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all UBOs, directors, and authorized signatories against the following lists: (1) Hong Kong Monetary Authority's Sanctions List (UN sanctions implemented under the United Nations Sanctions Ordinance, Cap. 537); (2) United Nations Security Council Consolidated List; (3) OFAC Specially Designated Nationals (SDN) List and Sectoral Sanctions Identifications (SSI) List; (4) EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List; (5) UK HM Treasury Consolidated List; (6) Mainland China's Ministry of Public Security list of terrorist organizations; (7) World Bank Listing of Debarred Firms. Enhanced due diligence (EDD) is required for any PEP (politically exposed person) as defined by FATF, including family members and close associates. Screening must be performed at onboarding and continuously via automated real-time alerts. For this medium-risk industry (digital advertising media arbitrage), additional scrutiny on source of funds and business counterparties is mandated. All screening results must be documented and retained for at least 5 years.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Hong Kong Companies Registry's 'Name Search' and 'Certificate of Incorporation' application via the e-Registry portal (www.e-registry.gov.hk)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The company name may be in English, Chinese, or both. If Chinese, it must be in Traditional Chinese characters (not Simplified). The English name must be in Roman letters. For a WFOE in Mainland China, the Chinese name must be approved by the State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR) and must follow the format: [Administrative Division] + [Distinctive Name] + [Industry] + [Company Type]. The Hong Kong name must not be identical or confusingly similar to any existing name in the Hong Kong Companies Registry. Transliteration from English to Chinese must be phonetically consistent and not misleading. The four-tier naming convention for Mainland China requires: (1) administrative region, (2) trade name, (3) industry description, (4) legal form (e.g., 'Limited' or 'Co., Ltd.').

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Company Law of the People's Republic of China (2023 Revision, effective 1 July 2024), Articles 4, 14, 16, 23-26, 34, 50-54, 66, 74, 82, 95 and 109; Foreign Investment Law of the People's Republic of China (effective 1 January 2020), Articles 6, 10, 12 and 13; Negative List for Foreign Investment Access (2024 Edition); Regulations on the Administration of Company Registration
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR) and the local District/Municipal Market Supervision Administration; foreign-invested company registration is completed through the SAMR integrated online registration portal or the local Government Services Center
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Application for Registration of a Company (foreign-invested limited liability company) together with the Chinese-language Articles of Association; the authoritative output instrument is the Business License of a Legal Person with the Unified Social Credit Code
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: None. There is no minimum paid-up capital requirement for a WFOE under the PRC Company Law (2023) or Foreign Investment Law, provided the business is outside the Negative List. The registered capital and contribution schedule are set out in the Articles; shareholders must contribute in full within five years of incorporation unless a shorter period is specified. No blocked escrow account is legally required. Foreign currency capital must be remitted through the bank that handles the foreign exchange registration and the capital account.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the following acts, documents and appointments are approved and adopted as the first resolution of the Board of Directors of the Company, a wholly foreign-owned enterprise organized under the Company Law of the People's Republic of China, effective upon the date of issue of the business license. 1. Share Capital Subscription. The registered capital of the Company shall be the amount set out in the Articles of Association, being divided into ordinary shares of the class and nominal value described in the Articles. The founding shareholder shall subscribe for such shares and shall contribute the subscribed capital in accordance with the capital contribution schedule in the Articles, using freely convertible foreign exchange or RMB as permitted by law. The Board accepts the subscription and adopts the capital contribution schedule. The Board shall procure the opening of a registered capital collection account if any bank or regulatory authority requires one, but no blocked escrow account is otherwise required by law for the Company's digital advertising services. 2. Banking Authorization. The managing director and the authorized signatories designated by the Board are hereby authorized to open, maintain, and close bank accounts in the Company's name with any licensed commercial bank in China. The authorized signatories shall consist of the legal representative, the general manager, and one additional officer designated in writing. All payments above RMB [•] or the foreign-currency equivalent shall require two authorized signatures. The bank mandate shall continue until the Board revokes or modifies it by subsequent resolution. 3. Registered Office Adoption. The registered office of the Company shall be the address identified in the Articles of Association, and the Board adopts such address as the Company's registered office in China. The legal representative and the general manager are authorized to execute and deliver the office lease, to file all post-registration change notices, and to receive all regulatory and judicial process at such address. 4. Statutory Officers. The Board appoints [Name] as Legal Representative, [Name] as General Manager, [Name] as Executive Director, and [Name] as Supervisor. Each appointment is subject to the qualifications in the Company Law. The supervisor is independent of the day-to-day management. The officers shall hold office until the next annual meeting or until their successors are appointed. 5. General Authority. Each officer and director is authorized to execute all documents, forms, declarations, and instruments required to register the Company with market regulation, tax, foreign exchange, banking, customs (if applicable), and statistics authorities and to do all lawful acts required to give full effect to these resolutions.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Name Pre-Approval and Foreign Investment Negative List Screening
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR) National Integrated Enterprise Registration Portal and local Market Supervision Administration
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the pre-approval application through the SAMR online integrated service portal using the jurisdiction where the registered office will be located. Provide a clear description of the proposed business scope, namely digital advertising media arbitrage and affiliate lead generation corresponding to ISIC 7310 and NAICS 541810. The foreign investor must supply certified corporate identity documents and a legal opinion confirming that the scope is not subject to the Foreign Investment Negative List or sector-specific restrictions. SAMR will check the proposed Chinese company name for conflicts with prior registrations and mark the name as reserved for six months. If additional local prohibitions apply, SAMR will issue a formal notice requiring clarification before incorporation.
required_dossiers: Signed Application for Pre-approval of Enterprise Name
Certified copy of foreign investor's Certificate of Incorporation or business registration
Power of attorney granted to the local formation agent or authorized representative
Chinese translation of the investor's constitutional documents and board resolution
Statement confirming the proposed scope is outside the Foreign Investment Negative List
Passport photocopies of legal representative and supervisor
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is rejected or the scope query is raised, submit up to three alternative names and a legal opinion within 10 working days; if SAMR rejects the scope as impermissible, amend the scope to conform to ISIC 7310 and re-file the application through the online portal; an administrative reconsideration may be filed if the rejection is final.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Notarization, Legalization, and Preparation of Statutory Constitution Documents
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notary Public Office in the foreign investor's jurisdiction; Chinese Embassy/Consulate where required; certified translation agency; local SAMR documents acceptance window
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Notarize the foreign investor's registration certificate, the board resolution of the foreign investor authorizing the WFOE formation, and the identity documents of the proposed legal representative. If the foreign investor is domiciled in Hong Kong SAR, the documents may be notarized by a licensed Hong Kong notary and verified through the Chinese Services (Hong Kong) attestation mechanism; if domiciled elsewhere, obtain an apostille or consular legalization. Once notarization is complete, a certified translation company must prepare a Chinese translation of every constitutive document. Draft the Articles of Association in strict compliance with the Company Law, specifying the capital contribution schedule, governance structure, legal representative, supervisor, and registered office, and ensure that the draft is signed by all initial shareholders or their authorized representatives.
required_dossiers: Foreign investor's incorporation or registration certificate notarized and legalized/apostilled
Board resolution of the foreign investor authorizing WFOE formation
Power of attorney to the authorized representative
Draft Articles of Association in Chinese signed by all initial shareholders
Proposed capital contribution schedule and registered capital amount
Lease agreement for registered office or certificate of location from the lessor
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If notarization or legalization is rejected or considered incomplete, re-authenticate the documents using the correct Chinese consular route or apostille service, and provide a certified Chinese translation by a qualified translator; if translations are challenged, engage a notarized translator and resubmit within 15 working days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Submission of Incorporation Dossier and Issuance of Business License
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Local District or Municipal Market Supervision Administration (SAMR) online all-in-one platform or Government Services Hall
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the full incorporation dossier through the local SAMR's online platform, or in person at the District/Municipal Government service hall, under the jurisdiction of the Hong Kong-invested WFOE. The legal representative and supervisor must sign the application, Articles, and associated declarations via the SAMR digital certificate or by attending the counter in person. SAMR will review the compliance of the Articles with the Company Law, the conformity of the company name, and the legality of the registered capital. If the dossier is complete, SAMR will issue the Business License with the Unified Social Credit Code and generate a registration record in the National Enterprise Credit Information Publicity System. Applicants must then make an electronic filing of the license details and mandatory company announcements.
required_dossiers: Completed Application for Registration of a Company (SAMR Form)
Name Reservation Notice
Chinese Articles of Association signed by shareholders
Legal representative appointment certificate and identification documents
Supervisor appointment certificate and identification documents
Registered office lease agreement and proof of address
Foreign investor's notarized and legalized identity documents
Unified Social Credit Code registration form
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the application is returned with corrections, remedy the specific items and resubmit via the online queue; if the application is suspended because of suspected nonconformity, submit a written explanation within 5 working days; if the final decision is adverse, apply for administrative reconsideration with the superior SAMR authority or file an administrative lawsuit in the competent people's court.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Post-Registration Tax, Social Insurance, and Foreign Exchange Filing
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: State Taxation Administration local tax bureau; Human Resources and Social Security Bureau; State Administration of Foreign Exchange (SAFE) through appointed banks
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Within 30 days after obtaining the Business License, the Company must complete tax registration with the State Taxation Administration local office, social-insurance registration with the Human Resources and Social Security Bureau, and foreign-exchange registration with the SAFE-approved bank if the foreign investor will make a capital contribution. The legal representative or the finance officer should submit the unified social credit code, the lease agreement, the capital contribution schedule, and identification. The tax bureau will set up the entity's tax profile for corporate income tax, value-added tax, stamp duty, and payroll withholding. If the bank account is opened before foreign exchange registration, the account will be recorded and the bank may process the capital remittance only after the Company passes the enhanced due diligence and economic-beneficiary-ownership verification.
required_dossiers: Business License original and copy
Unified Social Credit Code certificate
Tax registration form covering corporate income tax, VAT, stamp duty and payroll withholding
Legal representative and finance officer identification documents
Registered office lease agreement
Bank account opening certificate after basic account is opened
Foreign exchange registration form or capital account application if foreign capital is injected
Social insurance registration form and staff list
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If tax registration is queried or delayed, submit the missing supporting documents through the tax service hall electronic folder and request a formal acceptance statement; if the foreign-exchange filing is rejected for AML or beneficial-ownership reasons, file an enhanced compliance packet and, if necessary, apply to SAFE for a ruling through the appointed bank; if late-registration penalties are assessed, apply for first-violation waiver or administrative reconsideration.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Bank Account Activation, Seal Engraving, and Operational Compliance Ratification
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Licensed commercial bank in China; Public Security Bureau-authorized seal engraving unit; SAMR online platform; Ministry of Industry and Information Technology for record-filing if applicable
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After the business license is issued, the Company must open a basic deposit account at a licensed commercial bank in the area of the registered office. The legal representative should appear at the bank with the original seal and license to complete the application and sign a two-signatory mandate approved by the Board. Simultaneously, obtain the company seal, financial seal, invoice seal and legal representative seal through a licensed seal engraving company registered with the Public Security Bureau. The Board must ratify the first board resolution and keep it in the corporate records. If the Company operates a digital advertising platform, file the required MIIT record filings and keep the AML enhanced-due-diligence package current. Only after these steps may the Company issue commercial invoices and commence transactions.
required_dossiers: Original Business License
Bank account application forms and board resolution on signatory authority
Legal representative and authorized signatories identification cards or passports
Company seal engraving certificate and Public Security Bureau approval
First board resolution ratification document
AML beneficial ownership declaration and expected transaction volume schedule
Tax invoice application form if applying for invoice issuance
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If bank onboarding is delayed by enhanced due diligence, deliver a supplementary compliance memorandum containing source of funds, business model, expected transaction volumes, and customer onboarding policies; if the seal engraving is queried by the Public Security Bureau, provide the stamp certificate and confirm the legal representative's identity in person; any suspension should be cured by completing the official correction checklist within the period stated in the rejection notice.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not Applicable - no industrial licensing board or municipal agency has jurisdiction because ISIC 7310 is a pure digital advertising and consulting service, not manufacturing, chemical, assembly, or warehousing. If the company later hosts production or physical logistics, the competent authority would be the Ministry of Industry and Information Technology (MIIT) and the local Market Supervision Administration.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Not Applicable - no manufacturing, operating, or physical license is required for pure digital affiliate media buying. The only sectoral digital formalities are an ICP filing and, if applicable, a network advertising compliance filing, which are not physical operating licenses.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Not Applicable - Ministry of Ecology and Environment (MEE) and provincial Ecology and Environment Bureaus have no registration requirement for a non-industrial digital advertising service.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt/Not Applicable (Category not listed; no EIA registration or full Environmental Impact Report required).
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not Applicable - zero industrial wastewater discharge, zero volatile organic compound emissions, and zero hazardous waste generation; only ordinary domestic office sewage is covered by the building's municipal sewage connection, and no industrial discharge permit is required.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Not Applicable - no Civil Defense fire permit, structural load inspection, or special workplace-safety approval is required for an office-based digital advertising company. The Company must maintain the landlord's fire-safety acceptance certificate and adopt a basic office fire-evacuation plan. If office alterations affect the building envelope, a simple interior-decoration fire-safety filing with the district fire rescue authority may be required.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: State Taxation Administration (STA) of the People's Republic of China; official electronic filing and invoice systems are administered via the national Electronic Taxpayer Service Platform (e-Tax) and the National VAT Invoice Verification Platform at etax.chinatax.gov.cn.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Step 1: The PRC-incorporated WFOE is registered with the State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR), which issues a Business License bearing the 18-digit Unified Social Credit Code (USCC); the USCC is the statutory Tax Identification Number/VAT identification code for the WFOE, and no separate TIN certificate is issued. Step 2: Within 30 days after the Business License is issued, the WFOE must complete tax registration information confirmation and supplement through the e-Tax portal, including legal representative and financial officer real-name authentication, registered address, banking details, and capital structure; the China tax authority receives the business registration data directly through the one-license-one-code data sharing platform. Step 3: The WFOE must file for VAT identification and elect its VAT classification: general VAT taxpayer or small-scale VAT taxpayer; if annual taxable turnover exceeds CNY 5,000,000 or the WFOE intends to claim input VAT credits or export zero-rating, it must apply for general VAT taxpayer registration. Step 4: The WFOE must register for the electronic invoice service platform, obtain electronic invoice quotas, and integrate its billing/ERP system with the STA-approved Fully Digitalized Electronic Invoice (FDEI) interface or use the web-based e-invoice module. Step 5: If the WFOE exports goods, it must separately register with China Customs via the China International Trade Single Window, obtain an operating customs registration code, and maintain the customs ten-digit code for export declarations. Step 6: A foreign non-resident entity such as the Hong Kong parent company is not issued a PRC USCC or VAT ID for the WFOE; a non-resident enterprise deriving PRC-sourced income must instead complete tax file number filing through the withholding agent or direct registration under the non-resident tax registration rules, and may separately apply for treaty benefits, before any PRC-source payments are remitted overseas.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: None. PRC law does not provide a check-the-box or hybrid-mismatch pass-through election; the WFOE is inherently a resident enterprise subject to entity-level Enterprise Income Tax and is a separate VAT taxpayer. The only material election is the voluntary registration as a general VAT taxpayer before reaching the CNY 5,000,000 turnover threshold where the simplified small-scale taxpayer levy would otherwise apply.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value-Added Tax (VAT) under the PRC VAT Law, the VAT Implementing Rules, and the STA's cross-border zero-rated/exempt services catalogue; the mainland WFOE is a PRC VAT taxpayer, separate from Hong Kong's territory-based taxation.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: CNY 5,000,000 annual taxable turnover (excluding VAT) is the mandatory threshold for general VAT taxpayer registration; a WFOE below this threshold is ordinarily treated as a small-scale VAT taxpayer at the simplified levy rate, but may voluntarily register as a general VAT taxpayer to recover input VAT and access zero-rating.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: The WFOE must issue all VAT invoices through the STA-administered Fully Digitalized Electronic Invoice (FDEI) system or the legacy tax-controlled invoice management module integrated with the Golden Tax Phase IV system. Invoice data is transmitted to the tax authority in real time; each invoice receives a unique 20-digit invoice number, an anti-fraud QR code, and a tax-control digital seal before delivery to the buyer is permitted. High-volume entities must use the STA-certified API/interface for automated invoice creation, rejection, and red-letter reversal; manual paper invoices outside the tax-control system are not VAT-valid and do not support input VAT credit or export zero-rating.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: For physical exports of goods, 0% VAT is available when the goods are loaded and exported from PRC customs territory under a valid Customs Export Declaration, the exporter and supplier are the same general VAT taxpayer, payment is received in convertible foreign currency from outside mainland China, and export proceeds are settled through a designated bank under State Administration of Foreign Exchange (SAFE) rules within the statutory deadline. For services, 0% VAT applies only if the WFOE supplies a service that falls within the STA's published Catalogue of Zero-rated Cross-border Taxable Services, the service is supplied to an overseas recipient, the service is wholly consumed outside mainland China, the contract, fund flow, invoice flow and any relevant documentation are consistent, and the WFOE keeps the substantiating export dossier for audit. Advertising, affiliate media-buying and lead-generation services are not automatically zero-rated; if classified as advertising services consumed abroad, they may instead qualify for VAT exemption rather than 0% zero-rating, which does not carry input VAT refund rights. To use 0%, the service arrangement should be documented as a qualifying business-process management or similar zero-rated service, if the factual substance supports that classification.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (Export Goods Declaration / Bill of Entry) with customs release and export clearance data from the China International Trade Single Window
Bill of Lading or air waybill/cargo receipt evidencing physical export outside the PRC customs territory
Inward Remittance Certificate (FIRC) or SAFE-authorized bank export-proceeds collection and settlement record evidencing receipt of export consideration in freely convertible foreign currency
Signed cross-border service agreement and zero-rated service declaration (for qualifying services) evidencing an overseas recipient and consumption of the service outside mainland China
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The STA and China Customs use Golden Tax Phase IV to match customs export declarations, electronic VAT invoices, foreign-exchange settlement records and corporate tax returns. If the foreign-exchange consideration is not repatriated within 180 days, or if any document in the substantiation bundle is false, missing or internally inconsistent, the zero-rate is retrospectively reversed, the supply is recharacterized as domestic taxable supply subject to 6% VAT (or the applicable goods rate), and the taxpayer must repay any VAT refund/input credit previously taken plus late-payment surcharge at 0.05% per day. Administrative penalties range from 50% to 500% of the tax underpaid or refund fraudulently obtained; serious export-refund fraud carries criminal liability under the PRC Criminal Law, suspension of refund eligibility, loss of general VAT taxpayer status, and customs credit-rating downgrade.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: People's Bank of China (PBOC) and the State Administration of Foreign Exchange (SAFE)
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: China maintains a managed floating exchange rate system. The RMB is current-account convertible but capital account operations are still largely administered. For the WFOE, daily operating transactions such as payment for advertising services receive automatic current-account processing once the bank validates the underlying contract, tax filings and invoice. Dividends can be remitted outward after the annual audit confirms distributable profit, the corporate income tax has been settled, and a 5% withholding tax under the mainland-HK double tax arrangement has been paid; the bank will accept the remittance as a current account transaction without pre-SAFE approval. In contrast, all FDI injections into the WFOE are capital account items. They require a Foreign Exchange Registration Certificate, a designated capital account with a licensed bank, and confirmation of paid-in capital by a chartered auditor. Long-term outward direct investment from the WFOE likewise is subject to prior SAFE and MOFCOM registration. Conversion limits were historically tight, but the current regime allows settled funds to be kept in RMB without a mandatory surrender ratio. The enterprise must still comply with macro-prudential parameters, including the restriction that capital funds cannot be used for speculative securities investment or entrusted loans to related companies without prior approval. The overall convertibility framework provides operational freedom for trade and service-related flows while retaining robust administrative controls over the capital account to prevent short-term speculative pressure and maintain financial stability.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Export proceeds, including service trade receipts from media buying, must be repatriated into the WFOE's domestic foreign exchange settlement account within 90 calendar days from the date of export service invoice issuance or customs declaration for physical goods. The current SAFE total-amount monitoring framework does not specify a fixed mandatory conversion ratio; an enterprise may retain foreign currency up to its SAFE-approved retention quota, which is typically based on the prior year's trade revenues. All amounts above that quota are mandatorily settled into RMB through the designated bank. No exporter is permitted to leave export proceeds outside the PRC unless a specific SAFE relaxation has been granted for an approved offshore account. Each receipt must be matched to the corresponding export declaration or service trade invoice in the bank's monitoring module within 30 days of receipt, and unmatched entries are flagged as regulatory exceptions.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account for FDI and RMB Basic Deposit Account

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Industrial and Commercial Bank of China Limited (ICBC)
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: RMB Basic Deposit Account and Foreign Exchange Settlement Account
SAFE-Registered Capital Account and Operational RMB Account
Basic Operational Currency Account and Capital Escrow Account

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low. Offshore fintech EMIs such as Mercury, Wise and Revolut Business are not licensed by the PBOC or SAFE to open bank settlement accounts or to conduct foreign exchange settlement for a China-registered WFOE. Their balances are not recognized as legal deposits for Chinese regulatory purposes and cannot be used for SAFE foreign exchange registration, capital settlement, tax filing or regulatory reporting. The WFOE must maintain its primary operational and capital accounts with an onshore licensed foreign-exchange designated bank. EMIs may at best serve as supplementary payment instruments for minor operating expenses, but their inability to handle FDI purpose codes, SAFE filings and tax withholding makes them legally and operationally non-viable as the main clearing infrastructure.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: China's PBOC bank settlement account administration rules require the WFOE's statutory director or legal representative to appear physically in-branch for opening the basic deposit account in most Tier-1 banks. Remote consular proxy opening is generally not permitted; the bank may accept a notarized power of attorney authorizing an in-branch representative, but the legal representative must still pass a recorded video interview conducted by the bank's compliance officer. For the SAFE-registered capital account, the legal representative or a written appointee with a notarized mandate may appear on behalf of the company. Final decisions rest on each bank's internal KYC policy; foreign legal representatives are expected to provide biometric passport information, proof of Hong Kong residency, and source-of-wealth details for the ultimate beneficial owners.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Opaque holding structure where the Hong Kong parent has nominee shareholders and the WFOE does not clearly disclose a natural person UBO
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified true copies of HK Company Search, Certificate of Incorporation, Business Registration, incumbency certificate, share register, board resolution approving the FDI, notarized UBO declaration showing the full ownership chain to natural persons, valid passports of every shareholder holding more than 10%, and source-of-wealth statements for each ultimate beneficial owner

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Affiliate media buying matches high-risk patterns of round-tripping payments to offshore advertising platforms without verifiable commercial substance
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Executed media buying and advertising placement contracts, publisher network agreements, affiliate program terms, campaign budget and media plan, invoices from overseas counterparties, independent traffic and conversion analytics, and at least six months of prior WFOE bank statements linking receipts to actual ad placements

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: FDI capital injection from Hong Kong arrives in the capital account without proper SAFE registration or with inconsistent purpose codes
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: SAFE FDI Foreign Exchange Registration Certificate, certified capital verification report issued by a Chinese CPA, Hong Kong parent board minutes approving the subscription, source-of-funds evidence from the parent's audited financial statements, MT103 with explicit FDI purpose code, and an encumbrance-free letter on the contributing shareholder's equity

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident legal representative and proxy signatory create identity ambiguity and mandate risk at the bank's KYC desk
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Notarized and consular-legalized power of attorney naming an onshore authorized agent, valid passport of the legal representative, valid passport and proof of residential address for the authorized agent, executed AML/KYC questionnaire outlining expected inbound and outbound flow patterns, counterparty geographies and business rationale

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: The Hong Kong parent must wire registered capital via SWIFT MT103 or via CIPS for RMB injection into the WFOE's SAFE-registered foreign exchange capital account. The SWIFT field 70 must carry the exact FDI purpose code and the SAFE FDI registration number. The receiving onshore bank, after verifying the remittance against the company's subscribed capital and business scope, will complete the SAFE admissions entry in the digital foreign exchange system and release the funds for conversion. Capital verification is performed either by the bank under the capital settlement under authenticity procedure or by a Chinese CPA who issues a formal capital verification report confirming the paid-in capital. The RMB funds resulting from settlement are credited to the operational RMB account and must be spent strictly in accordance with the WFOE's business scope; no speculative investments or unauthorized lending are permitted.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Digital advertising and media-buying disbursements are service trade payments and should be executed via SWIFT MT103 with the correct SAFE service trade purpose code for advertising and media services, such as 222020. The bank requires a service trade foreign exchange payment application form, the underlying contract, the invoice from the foreign payee, proof of withholding tax payment or tax clearance, and an internal compliance check that the beneficiary is not sanctioned. For physical-goods campaigns involving promotional merchandise, a commercial letter of credit or documentary collection can be routed through the bank's trade finance desk, but the standard rail for intangible media, affiliate commissions and lead generation fees remains SWIFT MT103. All outbound payments must be reported through SAFE's direct reporting system; self-clearing through an offshore EMI is not permitted for regulatory or audit purposes.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Onshore deliverable foreign exchange forward contracts for CNY/USD, CNY/HKD and CNY/EUR, limited to genuine current and capital account exposure such as ad-buying invoices, subscription payments and dividend remittances, executed with a designated SAFE-licensed bank and not exceeding the exact notional value of the underlying commercial transaction.

Cross-currency swaps for balancing CNY/HKD and CNY/USD exposure on registered capital and dividend flows, booked after the bank verifies the actual debt or equity liability and completes the required SAFE macro-prudential filing.

FX options, both calls and puts, used solely to hedge the WFOE's exposure to currency volatility on confirmed trade invoices and dividend distributions, without embedded leverage beyond the underlying exposure.

Offshore CNH non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) cannot be transacted by the mainland WFOE because SAFE onshore rules permit only deliverable hedging products; the Hong Kong parent may use CNH NDFs to hedge its consolidated equity exposure but the WFOE itself is confined to onshore deliverable instruments.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Return (NAR1) for private company limited by shares
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Companies Registry of Hong Kong SAR
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 42 days after the anniversary date of incorporation; anniversary rule under Section 662 of the Companies Ordinance (Cap. 622)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Scale of late filing fees: HKD 870 if over 42 days up to 3 months; HKD 1,740 if over 3 up to 6 months; HKD 2,610 if over 6 up to 9 months; HKD 3,480 if over 9 months; additionally the company and every responsible officer are liable to prosecution and, on conviction, to a fine; the Registrar may strike the company off the register for persistent default.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On or before expiry of the current business registration certificate; the renewal notice is issued one month before expiry, and the fee must be paid within the prescribed window (usually by the expiry date)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late payment attracts a late fee of HKD 300; non-payment may lead to a fine not exceeding HKD 3,000 and prosecution under the Business Registration Ordinance (Cap. 310).

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Profits Tax Return (BIR51) with audited financial statements and tax computation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within one month from the date of issue of the return; for electronic filing by an authorized tax representative, the IRD may extend the deadline to up to three months depending on the accounting period and filing schedule
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file without reasonable excuse is an offence with a fine up to HKD 10,000; the IRD may make an estimated assessment equal to at least 8.25% of estimated income; interest may be charged on overdue tax; continued default may lead to prosecution with a further fine of HKD 20,000 and a daily fine.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Employer's Return (BIR56A) and individual employee remuneration forms (BIR56B/BIR56C etc.)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within one month of the issue date; the return is usually issued on the first working day of April each year for the preceding year of assessment
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Willful failure to file is an offence under the Inland Revenue Ordinance (Cap. 112) with a maximum fine of HKD 10,000 and imprisonment for three years; a separate penalty for late filing of HKD 10,000 may be imposed.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual General Meeting and laying of audited financial statements before members
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Members/shareholders of the company (internal corporate organ; enforced by the Companies Registry)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: For a private company, the AGM must be held within nine months after the end of the company's accounting reference period (18 months for the first accounting reference period); audited financial statements, with the balance sheet and profit and loss account, must be laid before the AGM
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Every director in default is liable to a maximum fine of HKD 300,000 under the Companies Ordinance and, for continuing contravention, a daily fine of HKD 2,000; alternate compliance may include written resolution if all members agree.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: All Hong Kong private companies limited by shares are required by Section 371 of the Companies Ordinance (Cap. 622) to prepare financial statements that give a true and fair view and to have those statements audited by a certified public accountant, unless the company is eligible for and validly claims audit exemption under Part 9. A private company (and its group, if applicable) is exempt for a financial year if it satisfies at least two of the following three criteria as at the balance sheet date: annual revenue not exceeding HKD 20 million; total assets not exceeding HKD 10 million; number of employees not exceeding 50. The exemption does not apply to companies whose constitutional documents, members, or shareholders require an audit, nor to companies carrying on regulated activities such as banking, insurance, securities, or money service operator activities. The audit threshold is therefore a reverse test: audit is compulsory unless the quantitative small-company exemption is available and a Section 356 resolution (or relevant exempt certificate) has been properly passed and filed with the Companies Registry.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Hong Kong Financial Reporting Standards (HKFRS) as issued by the Hong Kong Institute of Certified Public Accountants; the SME Financial Reporting Framework and Financial Reporting Standards (SME-FRS) may be applied by eligible private companies that meet the 'small-entity' criteria; group financial statements must comply with HKFRS unless an exemption applies.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Hong Kong applies a Significant Controllers Register (SCR) regime (Part 15A of the Companies Ordinance, Cap. 622). There is no annual UBO filing or annual confirmation to the Companies Registry; instead, a company must maintain an up-to-date SCR at its registered office or at a prescribed location, and any change in significant controllers (e.g. a share transfer that changes direct or indirect ownership of more than 25% of the shares or voting rights, or significant influence) must be recorded in the SCR within 7 days after the company becomes aware of the change. In addition, the company must respond to any query from a law enforcement officer or the Financial Services and the Treasury Bureau, and allow inspection of the SCR by authorized officers at any time. Failure to maintain or update the SCR is a criminal offence with a maximum fine of HKD 25,000 for each default, and a further daily fine of HKD 700 with up to two years' imprisonment for non-compliance.

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Qualified High-New Technology Enterprise (HNTE) rate: 15%; Small Low-Profit Enterprise preferential regime: 5% effective tax rate for qualifying taxpayers; R&D expenses: 100% additional deduction; Hainan Free Trade Port and Western Regions encouraged-industry substantive-operation enterprises: 15%; qualified software/IC enterprises may access two-year exemption plus three-year half-rate holiday; no automatic patent-box regime for pure media buying.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form A100000 (Annual Corporate Income Tax Return, Type A, 2017 version) together with schedules A105000, A108000/A109000, and the non-resident withholding schedule on the State Taxation Administration electronic tax-filing portal (e-Tax); quarterly provisional returns use Form A200000.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual final settlement with quarterly provisional payments
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Quarterly provisional returns within 15 days after each quarter end; annual final return within 5 months after the fiscal year-end (by 31 May for a calendar-year taxpayer); a non-calendar fiscal year requires advance approval.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Sales revenue from performance-based media buying and affiliate lead generation, reported net of VAT; includes advertising arbitrage and affiliate commissions recognized under PRC accounting standards.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report only arm's-length amounts when transacting with a Hong Kong affiliate; off-market payments must be adjusted and reconciled in related-party schedule A105000. No non-resident WHT is charged on inbound service income unless it constitutes Chinese-source royalty or the non-resident creates a PRC permanent establishment.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Cost of operations: media-buying inventory, traffic procurement costs, direct fulfillment costs, and technology-based campaign costs.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Cross-border traffic procurement paid to non-residents must be supported by contracts and invoices; embedded royalties for IP or software must be unbundled and subjected to 10% statutory WHT (treaty rate 5% for a qualifying Hong Kong beneficial owner) where the payment is in substance consideration for intellectual property.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxes and surcharges: urban construction tax, education surcharges, local education surcharge, stamp duty; excludes CIT and VAT.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Ensure VAT withheld on non-resident service imports is not incorrectly claimed as a deductible expense; all golden-tax invoice matching rules apply to media-buying disbursements.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Selling expenses: affiliate payouts, media placement commissions, customer acquisition costs, and brokerage fees.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Affiliate commissions paid to a connected Hong Kong company require transfer pricing benchmarking under CUP or TNMM; if the HK affiliate lacks employees, functions, risks, or a fixed place of business, the PRC tax authority may disallow the deduction or recharacterize the payment as a dividend subject to 10% WHT (treaty 5% only with substance).

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Administrative expenses: payroll, rent, professional fees, office overhead, IT infrastructure, and management fees.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Intercompany management fees paid to a Hong Kong related party are deductible only when services are actually rendered, the charge does not duplicate shareholder costs, and a complete cost-apportionment file exists; missing substance causes an add-back and possible deemed dividend treatment.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Financial expenses: bank charges, interest on borrowings, exchange losses, and guarantee fees.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Interest paid to the HK parent is deductible only if arm's-length, within the PRC thin-capitalization debt-to-equity ratio of 2:1 for non-financial enterprises, and not structured to avoid withholding; statutory WHT on interest is 10%, reduced to 7% under the Mainland-HK arrangement only after a valid beneficial-ownership filing.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Investment gains or losses, gains on disposal of assets, non-operating income and non-operating expenses, leading to total profit.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Do not net outbound dividend WHT against investment income lines; if the WFOE is liquidated, undistributed profits are treated as dividends to the HK shareholder and mandatory withholding applies; liquidation proceeds require Form A109000 filing.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Reconciliation of accounting profit to taxable income: disallowed expenses, tax-exempt income, loss compensation, and prior-year adjustments.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Transfer pricing adjustments, thin-capitalization interest add-backs, disallowed intercompany service fees, and GAAR recharacterizations are captured here; maintain the full Local File and Master File before filing, not only upon audit.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing under Tax Collection Law Article 62: penalty up to RMB 10,000 (RMB 2,000 standard; RMB 2,000-10,000 for serious/repeat offenders). Failure to pay within the deadline: daily late-payment surcharge of 0.05% on unpaid tax. False or fraudulent underpayment: 50%-500% penalty on the evaded amount plus daily surcharge. Criminal tax evasion under Criminal Law Article 201: imprisonment up to 3 years for a large amount exceeding 10% of tax payable, and 3-7 years for an enormous amount exceeding 30%; false-invoice crimes under Article 205 can reach life imprisonment in extremely serious cases. Serious tax offenders and their responsible legal representatives face blacklisting, exit-control travel bans, and joint-punishment restrictions.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 10% statutory PRC withholding on dividends paid by the WFOE to a non-resident shareholder; reduced to 5% under Article 10 of the Mainland-Hong Kong Double Taxation Arrangement if the Hong Kong company is the beneficial owner and directly holds at least 25% of the WFOE's paid-in share capital.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Before remitting dividends, the WFOE as withholding agent files the non-resident withholding return and claims treaty relief. The Hong Kong shareholder must provide a Tax Residency Certificate (TRC) issued by the Hong Kong Inland Revenue Department, complete the PRC beneficial-owner declaration, submit certificates of incorporation, shareholding
